Content:
When solving problems with angles, it is helpful to remember the following classifications:

Content:
- a null angle has a measure of [MATH: 0^\circ,]
- an acute angle has a measure between [MATH: 0^\circ] and [MATH: 90^\circ,]
- a right angle has a measure of [MATH: 90^\circ,]
- an obtuse angle has a measure between [MATH: 90^\circ] and [MATH: 180^\circ,]
- a straight angle has a measure of [MATH: 180^\circ,]
- a reflex angle has a measure between [MATH: 180^\circ] and [MATH: 360^\circ,] and
- a full angle has a measure of [MATH: 360^\circ.]

Content:
It is also helpful to remember that when two lines meet at a point, the opposite angles are called vertical angles. Vertical angles are congruent, and consequently they have the same measure.

  • Statement III is false. Angles [MATH: \angle A] and [MATH: \angle B] are not vertical since they have a common side.

So, the correct answer is "I only."

lesson.readable_text:
Item 1 — Tutorial: Introduction

Content:
When solving problems with angles, it is helpful to remember the following classifications:

Content:
- a null angle has a measure of [MATH: 0^\circ,]
- an acute angle has a measure between [MATH: 0^\circ] and [MATH: 90^\circ,]
- a right angle has a measure of [MATH: 90^\circ,]
- an obtuse angle has a measure between [MATH: 90^\circ] and [MATH: 180^\circ,]
- a straight angle has a measure of [MATH: 180^\circ,]
- a reflex angle has a measure between [MATH: 180^\circ] and [MATH: 360^\circ,] and
- a full angle has a measure of [MATH: 360^\circ.]

Content:
It is also helpful to remember that when two lines meet at a point, the opposite angles are called vertical angles. Vertical angles are congruent, and consequently they have the same measure.

---

Item 2 — Example: Identifying Angle Types From a Diagram

2. [MATH: \angle B] is a right angle
3. [MATH: \angle A] and [MATH: \angle B] are vertical angles

Content:
EXPLANATION

Explanation:
Let's examine our statements in turn.

- Statement I is true. From the diagram, [MATH: \angle A] and the angle with measure [MATH: 130^\circ] are vertical angles. Therefore,
[MATH: m\angle A = 130^\circ > 90^\circ.]
Consequently, [MATH: \angle A] is an obtuse angle.
- Statement II is false. From the diagram, [MATH: \angle B] and the angle with measure [MATH: 50^\circ] are vertical angles. Therefore,
[MATH: m\angle B = 50^\circ \neq 90^\circ.]
Consequently, [MATH: \angle B] is not a right angle.
- Statement III is false. Angles [MATH: \angle A] and [MATH: \angle B] are not vertical since they have a common side.

So, the correct answer is "I only."
